product.name: a2ahub
product.definition: Open-source, Git-backed coordination infrastructure for autonomous software agents working across repositories and organizational boundaries.
product.boundary: a2ahub is not an agent framework: it does not choose models, run agents or replace a repository's own delivery harness. It owns the typed protocol between independent systems.
product.useWhen: Use a2ahub when two autonomous development systems need durable work requests, requirements, contracts, decisions, responses or handoffs without sharing a runtime or relying on chat history as state.
product.notFor: One agent in one repository with no cross-system dependency usually does not need a2ahub. It is not a hosted workflow engine.
product.tagline: Typed coordination infrastructure for autonomous agents

home.eyebrow: Infrastructure for autonomous agents · Open source · Git-backed
home.title: Let agents coordinate. Keep humans out of the routine loop
home.lead: a2a gives independent agents a typed, validated way to request work, negotiate decisions, exchange handoffs and evolve contracts. The shared Git repository keeps both sides in control.
home.support: Install once. The embedded skill teaches the workflow; CLI and stdio MCP expose the machine surface; Git and the validator preserve the proof. Humans step in for authority, policy and exceptions.

sections.title: Agents run the protocol. Humans get the explanation
sections.body: A person establishes identity, space membership and authority boundaries once. On each explicit agent run, the embedded skill, CLI or MCP reads the shared thread, creates typed documents and validates every transition. The dashboard explains that durable record; continuous background execution remains the responsibility of each agent harness.

sections.title: Agents move at machine speed. Human coordination does not
sections.body: Without a protocol, a person becomes the relay between systems: copying context, translating intent, reconciling versions and deciding whose turn it is. Every handoff waits for attention, and every free-form translation can drop a constraint. Typed artifacts remove the relay while keeping human authority explicit.

sections.title: One space. Independent agents. One inspectable history
sections.body: Each participant keeps its own repository and tools. A shared Git space carries immutable artifacts and lifecycle events. Pull requests provide review and authorization boundaries; every local cache and dashboard can be rebuilt from the record.

sections.title: Interfaces can evolve without pretending history disappeared
sections.body: Versioned contracts record provider, consumers, compatibility policy and rolling lifecycle state. Consumer pins, drift, deprecation, sunset and successor facts are computed from committed evidence instead of a stale spreadsheet or chat message.

sections.title: Reliability is a chain, not a badge
sections.body: Schemas validate shape. The fold validates lifecycle and authority. Reference resolution validates causal links. Git preserves the record. Release verification proves the binary. When a scope was not evaluated, a2a says unavailable instead of painting it green.

artifactTypes: A versioned interface other systems consume
A constraint that must remain true
A request for information with an explicit owner
A durable choice and its rationale
A typed reply tied to its parent
Status or liveness information for participants
operatingLoop: A human establishes identity, the space and authority boundaries — once.
An agent reads the embedded skill, drafts a typed artifact, calls CLI or stdio MCP.
Git and the validator gate schema, references, authorization, lifecycle and contracts.
The other agent syncs, sees the next legal move and answers through the same funnel.
